content.text: I'll check every `deletedAt` reference in the app to confirm the changes are consistent.

Feature 3 (soft delete for comments) is built, but I could not run the tests or `prisma migrate deploy` here, so none of it is verified by execution.

**Answers to the questions**

1. A deleted comment keeps its row and gets a `deletedAt` timestamp. Comment lists show only comments whose `deletedAt` is null. Only the author can delete.
2. New error responses use `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. HTTP status codes stay as they are today: 422 for validation, 401 for a missing or bad token, 404 and 403 as before, and 500 for anything else.

**What changed (all under app/)**

- `src/prisma/schema.prisma`: added `deletedAt DateTime?` to `Comment`. It is nullable, so existing rows stay live.
- `src/prisma/migrations/20261030130000_comment_deleted_at/migration.sql`: adds the nullable column, with the undo line on top. I chose this timestamp so it sorts after feature 2's `20261030120000_comment_edited_at`.
- `article.service.ts`, `deleteComment`: the lookup also filters on `deletedAt: null`, and the code calls `update` to set `deletedAt` instead of `delete`. The 404 and 403 bodies are unchanged.
- `article.service.ts`, `getCommentsByArticle`: the comment query adds `deletedAt: null`.
- `src/tests/services/article.service.soft-delete.test.ts`: new unit tests with the Prisma mock. They cover the soft-delete write, the lookup filter, 404 for another user's comment and for an already-deleted comment, and the list filter.

**Rules applied**

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| soft-delete-behavior | Set `deletedAt` and keep the row. Leave deleted comments out of lists. Only the author may delete. | policy-soft-delete.md (team notes) |
| error-response-shape | `{"error":{"code","message"}}` for new errors. Status codes unchanged. | policy-error-response.md (team notes) |
| comment-ownership | Owner is `authorId`. Lookup is by id and author; not found or not the author gives 404 with an empty body. | code-comment-ownership.md, checked against `deleteComment` |
| comment-model-fields | Fields as in schema.prisma. `deletedAt` is nullable. | code-comment-model.md, checked against schema.prisma |
| auth-header | Used only as the source of the current user id. Not changed. | code-auth-header.md (team notes) |
| migration-and-release | One folder, timestamped name, one-line undo note at the top. Not yet run against a fresh database. | code-migrations.md, policy-release-checklist.md (team notes) |
| test-layout | Unit tests in app/src/tests/services, `*.test.ts`, using prisma-mock. | code-test-layout.md (team notes) |

**Conflicts and stale notes**

- **Error shape:** ops-runbook.md asks for the `errors`-by-field shape, and policy-error-response.md replaces it. I followed the policy, as the spec does. This feature adds no new error responses, so the new shape is not used in code. The existing 404 and 403 bodies stay as they are, per the spec's open points. The runbook still needs updating, and support may need to know.
- **Stale notes:** code-comment-model.md says there is no `editedAt`, but schema.prisma has one from feature 2's uncommitted work. The migrations note says four folders, but there are five, including feature 2's.

**Gaps I left alone**

- `updateComment` does not check `deletedAt`, so an author could still edit a comment they deleted, within the 30-minute window. This is outside the spec's four scope items, so I did not change it. It needs a decision.
- Feature 2's uncommitted edits sit in the same schema, service, and migration files. I added only my lines and did not touch its code.
